newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: U.S. chip data has little impact on Seoul bourse.
newsitem.headline: U.S. chip data has little impact on Seoul bourse.

text.p: Samsung Electronics gained strongly in early trading in Seoul but later fell back as investors digested news of an improvement in the U.S. seminconductor industry's key indicator, brokers said.
LG Electronics also shed early gains and the overall market was down fractionally. After 40 minutes the index dropped 3.05 points to 799.99.
Brokers said the index was likely to hover just below the psychologically-important 800 level as a recent technical rebound appeared to be burned out.

The U.S. Semiconductor Industry Association said the book-to-bill ratio rose to 0.9 in August, meaning for every $100 in shipments there was $90 of new orders. Seoul brokers said this did not mean the industry was out of the woods.
"The ratio has improved slightly but it does not mean that the market has turned around," said Kim Wan-hee, an analyst at Dongsuh Securities.
Samsung gained 700 won in the opening minutes but later eased. After about an hour it was down 1,000 won to 59,300. LG put on 200 won soon after the opening bell but was later flat at 14,800 won.
